status: Stored-block stage; Huffman paths retain development exits

steps.title: Reject unsupported counts before pointer access

quiz.prompt: Why is six the minimum outer input count?

choices.text: Two zlib header bytes and four checksum bytes require six bytes.
Every supported stream produces six pixels.
The bit reader always loads six bytes at once.

hints.text: Keep input and output counts separate.
Use unsigned comparisons without narrowing the arguments.

steps.title: Validate the zlib header and its advertised window

quiz.prompt: What does the window code bound?

choices.text: The number of bytes in IHDR.
The permitted backward match distance.
The framebuffer stride.

hints.text: Check method, window code, flags and header check separately.
Retain the derived history limit for the later match decoder.

steps.title: Reserve the checksum bytes from the bit reader

quiz.prompt: Where is the compressed-data end for a 46-byte zlib stream?

choices.text: At offset 46.
At offset 42, before the checksum.
At output offset 35.

hints.text: Use the input count to locate the trailer.
Use the expected output count only for the output end.

steps.title: Refill only from the compressed byte window

quiz.prompt: When does a zero-bit request require a refill?

choices.text: Always.
Only before the first block.
Never.

hints.text: Test available bits before loading another byte.
The compressed end deliberately excludes the trailer.

steps.title: Consume the low bits and retain the remainder

quiz.prompt: Does extracting three buffered bits advance the input cursor?

choices.text: Yes, by three bytes.
No; the earlier refill already consumed its byte.
Yes, by one output pixel.

hints.text: Mask before shifting away the consumed field.
Update bit count independently from byte cursor.

steps.title: Separate the final flag from the block type

quiz.prompt: What does field value one describe?

choices.text: A final stored block.
A nonfinal fixed block.
An already verified checksum.

hints.text: Separate one flag bit from the two type bits.
Do not treat an unfinished recognized handler as a malformed type.

steps.title: Discard stored-block padding before its length

quiz.prompt: What happens to the byte cursor during alignment here?

choices.text: It advances by five.
It moves back to the header.
It stays at the next byte already selected by refill.

hints.text: Discard buffered padding without rereading the header byte.
Keep alignment confined to stored blocks.

steps.title: Read LEN and NLEN as sixteen-bit fields

quiz.prompt: What follows from LEN XOR NLEN equaling 65535?

choices.text: LEN is necessarily within the output capacity.
The two stored length fields are complementary.
The complete Adler checksum is correct.

hints.text: Retain the first helper result before the second call overwrites it.
The length fields use the ordinary low-bit reader, not big-endian assembly.

steps.title: Check readable and writable payload extents

quiz.prompt: Which bounds must be established before copying?

choices.text: Only the source extent.
Only the destination extent.
Both source availability and destination space.

hints.text: Compare lengths with remaining counts before forming copy loops.
Do not let a valid complement stand in for a window check.

steps.title: Copy a stored payload exactly once

quiz.prompt: How many bytes does an empty stored block copy?

choices.text: Zero.
One padding byte.
Four checksum bytes.

hints.text: Test for the empty range before loading.
Advance the two byte cursors together for a stored payload.

steps.title: Continue nonfinal blocks without publishing success

quiz.prompt: What must survive a transition to another block?

choices.text: The accumulated output cursor.
The previous block length as the next length.
A claim of final success.

hints.text: Use the final flag retained when selecting this block.
Continue appending to the same output window.

steps.title: Require exact output and compressed-byte completion

quiz.prompt: Can matching Adler-32 replace the output-cursor equality?

choices.text: Yes, because checksums uniquely identify every byte sequence.
No; checksum agreement does not establish how many bytes were produced.
Yes, if the destination was prefilled.

hints.text: Check actual cursor positions, not just the requested counts.
Reject unread compressed bytes before treating the next four bytes as the trailer.

steps.title: Compute Adler over the produced row range

quiz.prompt: What does the Adler helper receive in its second argument here?

choices.text: The end address of the output range.
The compressed count.
The expected CRC.

hints.text: Use the updated first sum when advancing the second.
Only produced output belongs in this checksum.

steps.title: Read the reserved checksum in PNG stream order

quiz.prompt: Why not read the trailer with an ordinary native word load?

choices.text: Its four bytes are explicitly big-endian, independently of target order.
Its checksum contains eight bytes.
A native load always computes Adler automatically.

hints.text: Keep file byte order separate from native workspace fields.
The outer input bound and reserved end establish four readable trailer bytes.

quiz.prompt: Why can the bad-Adler fixture reach the inflater?

choices.text: The host helper preserves valid PNG chunk CRCs around the changed zlib stream.
The collector already decoded all rows.
The final checksum is ignored for stored blocks.

hints.text: Distinguish compressed-container checks from inflated-data checks.
Keep the failure return count zero even if row scratch contains all bytes.

quiz.prompt: Why does the whole program still print its development message?

choices.text: The inflater returned the wrong count.
Row reconstruction and framebuffer publication remain unfinished.
A stored block cannot contain PNG row bytes.

hints.text: Inspect the inflater return before the wrapper advances to the next unfinished stage.
Do not award a completed inflater grade while Huffman paths are missing.
